name: Mazabraud Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of fibrous dysplasia lesions in bone confirmed by imaging and/or histopathology
Presence of intramuscular myxomas confirmed by imaging and/or histopathology
Clinical symptoms consistent with fibrous dysplasia and soft tissue myxomas such as localized swelling or deformity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fibrous dysplasia lesions and at least one intramuscular myxoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on radiological and histopathological findings; genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Radiographs showing ground-glass appearance of fibrous dysplasia lesions
MRI demonstrating intramuscular myxomas with characteristic signal intensities
CT scans for detailed bone lesion assessment
other: Histopathology confirming fibrous dysplasia and myxoma tissue types

distinguishingFeatures: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia with endocrine abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of fibrous dysplasia lesion or myxoma
New onset neurological deficits suggestive of nerve compression
Signs of malignant transformation such as severe pain, swelling, or pathological fracture
references: Mazabraud A, et al. Fibrous dysplasia and intramuscular myxomas: a new syndrome? J Bone Joint Surg Br. 1967.
DiCaprio MR, Enneking WF. Fibrous dysplasia. Pathophysiology, evaluation, and treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2005.
Lichtenstein L. Fibrous dysplasia of bone. Arch Pathol. 1938.
